executive_summary: Approved unconditionally. I independently read the complete PM runbook, backend contracts and review schema, the controlling iteration-05 feedback, every iteration-01 through iteration-06 candidate/checksum/handoff/review artifact, the frozen iteration-06 candidate, and the post-CPI facts.json. I rehashed the exact 35,795-byte candidate to e67074adad21b42b12a947485ffd754b117c271f0a1488f20177bc325c2366d8, matching candidate.sha256 and pm-handoff.json, and verified the complete prior digest chain. Fresh independent Yahoo retrieval reproduced every finalized 09:46 one-minute bar, all full-precision September 10 and September 4 bases, every six-decimal return, rounded price, label, direction and timestamp for all ten instruments. The evidence collection at 09:47:23 occurred after the selected 09:46 bars closed, and candidate as_of at 09:47:28 followed collection. Fresh official and direct-source retrieval supports the policy, CPI, communications and active macro facts. Waller remains speech-only September 3 evidence and CPI remains a separate September 11 driver. The sensitive Fed scenario interpolation is arithmetically correct and explicitly non-direct; the BoC October distribution correctly remains unavailable and null under the quarterly-contract contract. All checks pass with no unresolved finding or instruction.

Official policy passes fresh direct retrieval. The BoC September 2 statement and upcoming-events page support the 2.25% overnight target, administered-rate context and October 28 09:45 decision/MPR.

CPI and communication separation passes. Fresh browser-impersonated BLS retrieval supports August headline CPI +0.4% monthly and +3.4% yearly and core +0.3% monthly and +2.4% yearly; the freshly collected FXStreet calendar rows support consensus +0.4%, +3.4%, +0.2% and +2.4% and priors +0.1%, +3.4%, +0.2% and +2.5%. The separate 1.5-weight CPI card is mixed-hawkish and numerically consistent. The Waller card contains only his September 3 conditional reaction function and through-July inflation discussion, retains the official 08:30 Toronto timestamp, and does not import the September 11 CPI result. Fresh speech retrieval supports continued-disinflation hold, hot-inflation hike consideration, only slightly restrictive policy, and the 4.76% to 3.05% three-month core-inflation comparison.

Fed pricing arithmetic and provenance pass. Fresh Yahoo retrieval reproduces the 09:35 ZQU26 bar at 96.27249908447266, and the NY Fed API reports EFFR 3.63%. These imply a 3.7275009155273438% monthly average, a 3.8389305332728796% post-decision rate, hold weight 0.16427786690848123 and hike weight 0.8357221330915188, matching the candidate's rounded 16/84 distribution and implied rate. This remains a highly sensitive adjacent-leg desk interpolation, not CME FedWatch or a directly measured distribution; zero cut is a model restriction and the candidate discloses both limitations.

BoC pricing passes the unavailable-state contract. cut_25bp, hold, hike_25bp and implied_rate_after are null; probability_status is unavailable; and an observable CRAU26 quarterly proxy is supplied without allocating it to October. Fresh TMX retrieval supports the 97.610 bid and 97.615 ask, whose 97.6125 midpoint implies a 2.3875% quarterly-average rate. The contract spans the October 28 and December 9 decisions, so it cannot identify a clean October distribution.

Fresh direct and official retrieval continues to support the unchanged material driver facts: revised JOLTS June 7.182M to July 7.271M, August payrolls +162k with July +21k and June +31k revisions, PPI +0.4%/+5.4% headline and +0.2%/+4.6% core, Warsh's inflation emphasis, Canada labour and wage weakness, asking-rent disinflation, and Q2 and June GDP resilience. The other active source-backed drivers and weights were reviewed in full; weights remain subjective and correlated evidence scores rather than independent probabilities.

Decision usefulness passes for these exact bytes: the snapshot clearly separates observed macro evidence, subjective rope weights, a mutable non-direct Fed pricing model, an unavailable BoC meeting distribution, and timestamped cross-asset validation. Remaining P&L limits are explicit: intraday prices and the Fed interpolation can move quickly, driver evidence is correlated, and this approval does not authorize carrying the snapshot through a later catalyst without a new freeze and exact-byte review.
